summary: Graves Mountain L-4 lookout cab on a 30-foot tower, moved piece by piece from the Colville National Forest to Colville in 1985 and now restored and open to the public.

facts.design: 30-foot timber tower with an L-4 cab measuring 14 by 14 feet; replaced an earlier pole tower on the mountain

access.note: The register says the restored lookout is open to the public daily; hours and climbing rules are not in the sources read.

events.note: Pole tower and log cabin built on the original Graves Mountain site by the U.S. Forest Service and the CCC in 1934; the historical society says early 1930s
A couple manned the lookout in 1944
Forest Service replaced the pole tower with a 30-foot timber tower and L-4 cab
Stevens County Historical Society moved the tower and cab piece by piece to Colville; the original site lost the tower that year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the former-lookout site record give the first pole tower as 72 feet; the historical society says 75 feet, and another lookout history site says 72 feet, possibly 80. The record stores no height for the first tower. height_m 9.1 is for the current 30-foot tower, converted from feet.

The historical society says the lookout station worked for almost 50 years; the register says the L-4 cab stood for 30 years, from 1955 to 1985. These describe different structures and spans, so the story reports both.

The register names the Stevens County Park and Museum; the former-lookout site record and another lookout history site say next to the Keller Historical Museum in Colville. The record keeps its Colville Museum name because both sites are in Colville.

The register places the lookout in Stevens County, where it now stands. The historical society and the former-lookout site record place the original mountain site in Ferry County. The record keeps Stevens County for the current lookout.

notes_for_editor: The NHLR lookout page gives coordinates and an elevation of 5,901 ft for the original mountain site (the former-site record gives 5,947 ft); the museum coordinates in the record are kept and no elevation is set. The former-site record (US 1449, WA 349, registered 2012) belongs to the sibling record us-wa-graves-mountain and is not merged here. The 1955-56 lookout names on WillhiteWeb are omitted for privacy; the 1944 couple is described without names. Search snippets from Visit Northeast Washington (Facebook, Instagram) say visitors can climb the stairs; those pages were not readable, so climbing is not stated. The WillhiteWeb sidebar (elevation 2,793 ft, Pend Oreille County) looks like another page's template and is not used. No photo URLs were added.
